#2798. Rhamondre Stevenson working to return sooner than expected

As the New England Patriots took the field for a walkthrough at the FC Bayern Munich Training Ground on Thursday, running back Rhamondre Stevenson was spotted working off to the side.

Stevenson missed Wednesday's practice in Foxboro with a knee injury that was initially reported to cause him to miss some time. His presence on the field in Germany, however, offers some optimism that the veteran running back could make a quicker-than-expected return for Sunday's matchup against the Detroit Lions.

"I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they're talking about a lot of the time," quarterback Drake Maye said of Stevenson's return. "And just a guy that wants to be out there, wants to be back for his team and we're in the midst of trying to make a make a run here and win a big one before the bye.

"This is a time for players, a lot of the players on this team that are trying to get out there, play with their teammates and knowing that he's a great player and can help us out."

Stevenson initially suffered the injury late in the third quarter of Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers after being brought down following a six-yard reception.

Reports indicated that Stevenson suffered a knee tendon issue near the back of his knee and while the injury was not expected to require surgery, he could miss the next few weeks. Stevenson, however, was upgraded to a limited participant Thursday which leaves open the possibility of a quicker return.

"He's a dawg, man," wide receiver DeMario Douglas said. "I know some people that probably be like, 'Man, I ain't even going to try', you but his situation, man, I be talking to him [and he's] like, 'I'm going to try. I'm going to do what I can do.' He's working, he's getting better. So, when the time comes, I know he's working to get better."

Stevenson's potential return would be a significant boost for a Patriots offense that has dealt with several injuries this season. He has been one of New England's most dependable players, logging 65% of the team's offensive snaps while piling up more than 650 total yards and four touchdowns. His contributions in pass protection have also earned consistent praise from teammates and coaches.

Potentially without Stevenson and with No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) already ruled out, the Patriots would be left with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. Terrell Jennings is also an option on the practice squad.

Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels made sure to note Stevenson's presence in Germany while also expressing confidence in whoever the team rolls out against the Lions on Sunday.

"Anytime you lose players like that, you feel it because he's such a valuable part of everything you do," McDaniels said. "But why we have a lot of guys that are taking reps in practice. We've had a lot of guys doing that all year long. They know what to do. It might not be the same volume of experience that certainly Rhamondre has, but we got a lot of guys in that room that we have confidence in… And Rhamondre is here too."

#2797. Banged-up squads square off in Raptors vs 76ers

Things have been a bit rough in Toronto as of late, with the Raptors suffering a spate of injuries to key players. They will again play without both Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard, as they did in Wednesday night's loss to the Boston Celtics. The date of Barnes's return is still TBD (Kawhi will undoubtedly be out for a while longer).

They've won just two of their last six and will be looking to hold down the fort on the second night of a back-to-back, all while missing some key players. The Raps will need young players like Ja'Kobe Walter and Collin Murray-Boyles to step up, especially if Barnes is still out. Can Toronto do enough on their own home court to keep their record from dipping below .500?

Unfortunately for Toronto, Philadelphia 76ers are off to a great start, but they've been a bit of an odd team so far. For all of their offensive talent — a starting lineup featuring LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, and Tyrese Maxey (not to mention Anfernee Simons off the bench) is absolutely bonkers — they're just 21st in the NBA in offensive efficiency so far this year.

They don't really shoot (or make) threes, partly a result of swapping Paul George for a more downhill player in Brown, and they don't generate extra opportunities by crashing the offensive glass. They're also surprisingly low in assists, especially considering the playmaking gifts of James and, to a lesser extent, Embiid, owed no doubt to some issues with spacing, a coach not exactly known for offensive ingenuity, and a lineup that's still largely unaccustomed to playing together.

It also doesn't help that Embiid is….well, if not cooked, then certainly in the process of being marinated. His recent injuries seem to have sapped him of his mobility and, while his skill is beyond question, you don't really ever want to see a 7-footer hitting just 37% of his shots from the field (nor a ghastly 12.1% from three), albeit in a small sample size.

They're also a bit thin aside from having a few useful perimeter players off the bench; their only actual backup centre is Adem Bona, who is shooting a whole percentage point better than Embiid from the field. Needless to say, they could use a boost on the interior. It's great news for the Raptors, who are a bit lacking in interior size themselves, and who aren't an especially good defensive rebounding team (23rd in the league in defensive rebound rate).

The Sixers have been a pretty solid defensive team though, with the seventh-best defensive rating in the league, and, while Embiid may not be able to switch onto guards anymore, he's still a smart defender who can be an obstacle in the paint. His declining lateral quickness is less of a disadvantage of a team like Toronto that doesn't space the floor exceptionally well.

These Sixers are very different from last year's team and this will be the first time they face off against the Bron-and-Brown version of Philly. That being said, the two teams split the season series last year, 2-2, with both squads winning once at home and once on the road.

LeBron and Embiid vs various ligaments might be the true matchup of the game. Both players are listed as questionable on the NBA's official injury report, as is Adem Bona. If neither of them play, Toronto won't exactly be facing a murderer's row of big men on Thursday night, with the Sixers almost certainly having to call players up from the G League or play some very funky small-ball lineups to get by. Maybe we'll get 30 minutes of Tacko Fall. Who knows!

Besides that, the Raptors will likely need RJ Barrett to outduel Brown, and Immanuel Quickley, who struggled to score against Boston, to keep pace with Maxey. It's not quite the marquee matchup fans hoped for after both teams' major offseason moves, but it could be a fun one nonetheless.

#2795. Marquette Men’s Basketball Announces Three Class Of 2027 Signees

Marquette men's basketball announced the official signing of all three of their Class of 2027 recruits on Wednesday. Marlon Martinez, Philipe Ndong, and Akol Nyok all turned in their paperwork on the first day of the fall signing period, and all three will arrive on campus in the summer of 2027 with five years of eligibliity.

Here's head coach Shaka Smart on the entire group:

"I'm ecstatic about the people and players that we're adding to our team," Smart said. "All three are true relationship guys – already hard at work building bonds with our staff and each other. Each possesses an exciting upside and commitment to what growth requires. All three play with a winning spirit that's exactly what we want at Marquette," Smart added.

Let's dive into each one, going in alphabetical order.

Martinez (6-foot-5, 200 lbs.) attends The Academy of Central Florida, which competes in The Grind Session, an elite winter circuit for top prep and high school basketball. Martinez formerly attended Bishop Loughlin High School in New York and has competed on Puma's Pro16 AAU circuit as a member of the Rhode Island Elite. A native of the Dominican Republic, he represented his home country at the 2026 FIBA U18 AmeriCup, where he averaged 19.0 points, 5.8 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game while shooting 48% from 3-point range.

"Marlon caught our attention the old-fashioned way – by being one of the best players in an event full of highly regarded prospects," Smart said. "Marlon's offensive game includes major versatility as a playmaker and play finisher.

"Inside his veins flows the DNA that will remind Marquette fans of winning big guards from previous eras – he competes and has flair," Smart added.

Martinez was the first of the three to commit to Marquette, making his announcement in early August. At the time, he was ranked not that far outside the top 100 by both 247 Sports and Rivals/On3, but a little deeper into the rankings in both sides' collective ranking systems because ESPN rated Martinez as only a three-start prospect. Today, 247 Sports has him at #95 internally and at #132 in their Composite rankings, while Rivals/On3 slots Martinez at #121 internally and #127 in their Industry rankings. ESPN is still the holdout here, but they only rank out to the top 100. The good news is that he's now a four-star prospect in their eyes.

Ndong (6-foot-9, 180 lbs.) plays under head coach Justin Perron at The Newman School in Boston, Massachusetts. Ndong was born in Malaga, Spain, and also lived in Turkey before coming to the United States. This past summer, he played for Middlesex Magic, the same AAU program that produced former Marquette star and current New York Knicks guard Tyler Kolek. He averaged 10 points and 2.3 rebounds while shooting 38% from 3-point range for Middlesex.

"Phil comes from a basketball background that is very unique and makes him a candidate for explosive growth, Smart said. His extremely high character and basketball IQ will make him a fast learner – and Phil loves taking on challenges.

"I'm predicting Phil and Todd Smith create a partnership very much like Todd and Oso (Ighodaro) from 2020-24," Smart added.

Ndong was a bit of a mystery at the time of his commitment in September, as 247 Sports and Rivals/On3 had an evaluation on him, but ESPN hadn't even conjured up a page for him at that point. 247 Sports has Ndong at #146 in their internal rankings right now, but up at #128 in the Composite. The reason why he moves upwards in the Composite is because Rivals/On3 slots Ndong in as the #56 prospect in the country. That's #6 amongst power forwards. Because 247 isn't matching their enthusiasm, the Rivals/On3 Industry Ranking lands Ndong at #112. ESPN has at least generated a page for him now, marking Ndong as a three-star prospect and ranking him as the 38th best power forward.

I think it's safe to say that we're all cheering for Rivals/On3 to be correct here.

Nyok (7-foot-1, 205 lbs.) is a native of South Sudan and currently resides in Miami, Florida. He attends Miami Columbus High School and is playing for the Cold Hearts in Overtime Elite, a nine-team basketball league in Atlanta, Georgia. So far this season, he is averaging 8.3 points, 9.3 rebounds and 1.3 blocks while shooting 60% from the field. Before Miami Columbus High School's basketball team joined Overtime Elite as the Cold Hearts, Nyok led the school to the 2026 Florida Class 7A state championship. Columbus defeated Sarasota 53-50 in the title game.

"Akol possesses two qualities that make his future in the program incredibly bright; he's on a terrific growth trajectory and his spirit for teammates and winning is second to none," Smart said. "Combine those with his length, athleticism and desire to be a special defender and we have a guy Marquette fans are going to enjoy getting to know."

Nyok was the third of the three to commit to the Golden Eagles, making his announcement in early October and generating the tiniest bit of consternation in the process. We'll get to it in a second. 247 Sports ranks him just outside the top 100 both internally (#104) and in the Composite (#107), and Rivals/On3 is much more excited. They have Nyok at #65 in their internal rankings and slotting him in as the #8 center prospect in the country. In the Industry rankings, he's #95 and #12 amongst centers. ESPN says he's a four-star prospect and 14th amongst centers. He can't be that far outside the top 100 at that rate, but the cut off line is the cut off line.

And here's the up to date scholarship chart, and then we'll get into the Nyok thing.

I will point your attention to the big red line between Philipe Ndong and Akol Nyok, as Marquette currently projects to be one player over the maximum roster limit of 15 for the 2027-28 season. At the time, I could only merely speculate about how Shaka Smart was going to solve this issue. Now that we're three games into the season, I can offer a much more informed statement.

The fact of the matter is that Ian Miletic has played 10 minutes across two of the games that Marquette has played this season and not at all against Michigan. Nash Walker has played even less, accruing just six minutes in MU's first two games before not appearing against the Wolverines. Colton Crowdis is over there in the minutes department with Braeden Brenn, who is not listed on the scholarship chart because he is grandfathered in under walk-on rules and can stick around as long as he wants/is eligible. There is no plan for any of these three to play anything resembling real minutes this season. If there was, Shaka Smart would have worked them into the rotation against Mercyhurst and Detroit Mercy, and that did not happen.

In Crowdis' case, I don't know why he's here at all. Miletic is at "can't play" status after a redshirt season of development. Walker at least has his shoulder surgery back in the spring to explain why he's not up to par, seeing as he wasn't cleared to play during the three game tour of Canada in early August, but it's still not a great sign that he's unplayable.

I'm not a fan of generating a discussion that even remotely approaches running a player out of town just because. However, I'm not the one signing players that puts the team over the roster limit while making it clear that three guys on the roster have no business on the roster at the moment. I'm just the one seeing this happen and pointing at it. This is going to get solved one way or another, and now we have to wait til April to find out precisely how.

#2792. Steph Curry to miss at least three NBA Cup games with abdominal tear

It's still unclear how long that Steph Curry's oblique abdominal tear will keep him off the court, though it will be two weeks at a minimum. But however long it is, the absence of their star will likely prevent the Warriors from competing for commissioner Adam Silver's most treasured piece of basketball hardware: The Emirates NBA Cup.

I mention the sponsor out of the deep and abiding respect we hold for all of the NBA sponsors, and particularly Commissioner Silver's good friends in the United Arab Emirates. The Cup has taken the basketball world by storm since it began in 2023, delighting fans and gamblers alike with its focus on point differential, and reminding a nation to check the color settings on their televisions thanks to the garish special courts.

Our personal favorite is the Los Angeles Lakers "Forum Blue and Urine" design, which showcases Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves on a court that makes it look like the Crypto.com Arena itself is severely dehydrated.

The Warriors are 1-0 in Cup play, but Curry's injury means he'll miss Friday's showdown with the San Antonio Spurs, who lost to the New York Knicks in last year's Cup final, the most significant Finals loss to the Knicks they'd suffer all season. Yes, Charles Bassey is prepared to go toe-to-toe with Victor Wembanyama, having proved his mettle against Marcus Smart, but it may be tough for the rest of the team to match the firepower of the Spurs and Harrison "The Black Falcon" Barnes.

It's hard to imagine Curry will be back to face the Sacramento Kings or the Portland Trail Blazers in two Cup games bracketing Thanksgiving, when families will gather together and express their gratitude for the mid-season tournament. It's not impossible that the Warriors could be 3-1 after that, but 2-2 is a more likely record, which wouldn't get the Dubs the wild-card spot. Even if they did get in, Curry would only be three weeks past his injury for the knockout rounds Dec. 4 and 5, and the Cup Final, held in glamorous Indianapolis, Indiana, is just one month away.

This is the gamble the Warriors made when they assembled a veteran roster this year in hopes they could make a serious Cup run. Sure, they could try to trade Kristaps Porzingis for immediate help, but are teams really going to help a possible Cup opponent this close to the knockout round? Yaxel Lendeborg has been a revelation as a rookie, but he's never had to prove himself under the Emirates NBA Cup spotlight.

The Knicks became the first team to win the double last season, taking home the NBA Cup and the Larry O'Brien trophy as NBA champions. The Warriors had a chance to be the first NBA team to win the "treble" — that is, Summer League, Emirates NBA Cup, and NBA titles. (As much as Adam Silver would like there to be, there's still no Champions League for the NBA)

Sure, Curry has five months to get ready for the regular NBA playoffs, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody also set to return. But for the hardcore Emirates-heads out there, it's looking like another lost NBA Cup season for the Warriors.

#2787. Charlie Villanueva, Raymond Felton debate Wemby vs. Michael Jordan scenario, because why not?

Charlie Villanueva, Raymond Felton debate Wemby vs. Michael Jordan scenario, because why not? appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The debate over the NBA's greatest players has taken another unexpected turn, with former players Charlie Villanueva and Raymond Felton weighing in on a hypothetical choice between Victor Wembanyama and Michael Jordan. Their discussion focused on which superstar a team should choose based on the first four seasons of their careers.

On their To The Baha podcast, Villanueva and Felton shared opposing views on the Wembanyama-Jordan comparison. Villanueva argued that Wembanyama's early career deserves a direct comparison with Jordan's, asking, "And don't say MJ because it's no way you're picking MJ, MJ didn't win until year what?" Felton immediately challenged that argument, pointing to Jordan's scoring numbers and Wembanyama's lack of a championship. "Michael Jordan averaged 35 points. Look at his numbers. Did Wemby win? I don't care. He didn't win," Felton said.

Jordan's fourth NBA season in 1987-88 was remarkable. He averaged 35.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 5.9 assists while winning the regular-season MVP and Defensive Player of the Year awards. Wembanyama, meanwhile, is averaging 30.3 points, 11.7 rebounds and 2.8 assists through 12 games in his fourth season.

However, Jordan had yet to win an NBA championship at that point. He captured his first title with the Chicago Bulls in 1991, during his seventh season. That timeline supports Villanueva's argument about judging players by their early-career production rather than their eventual championships.

Felton, meanwhile, puts greater emphasis on Michael Jordan's scoring dominance and individual accomplishments. The debate highlights two different ways of evaluating a player's career: individual production and team success. Victor Wembanyama still has time to build his legacy, but Jordan's fourth-season achievements give Felton a compelling case.

#2782. Myles Garrett’s stunning claim about winning Defensive Player of the Year

Myles Garrett had three sacks in his first game back from a two-month stint on injured reserve and the L.A. Rams edge rusher says that he plans to get a lot more than that. In fact, Garrett told Rich Eisen that he will specifically be looking to cross off the names ahead of him in sacks this year week by week and that he believes he can win Defensive Player of the Year in 2026 despite already missing seven games.

Given that he had 23 sacks last season, are Garrett's goals that crazy?

The NFL leader in sacks is Will Anderson, who currently stands at 9.5. "I don't plan to make it easy for (Anderson)," Garrett said on the Rich Eisen Show on Thursday.

Anderson's league-leading total is 1.5 sacks more than Gregory Rosseau and Chase Young in second place with eight each.

There are 11 players who have at least six sacks, which is twice as many as Garrett right now.

However, Garrett had three sacks last week. If he has three sacks this week against the Cardinals — a team starting Carson Beck in his NFL debut — he will already be knocking on the door of the top-10 heading into L.A.'s bye week.

#2777. The inside story of Manchester United's move for Mauricio Pochettino

MANCHESTER, England (AP) — In the end it came down to a choice of one.

From the moment Manchester United was aware of Mauricio Pochettino's availability he stood alone — the only candidate as the troubled Premier League club went in search of a new coach.

United's hierarchy had assumed Pochettino, like Aston Villa's Unai Emery, was out of reach.

Emery also has big admirers at United after transforming Villa from a relegation-threatened team to a serial Champions League challenger, a person with knowledge of the situation told The Associated Press on condition of anonymity to protect relationships. But the Spaniard, under contract and without a release clause, was simply not an option.

The same was thought of Pochettino after he signed a four-year deal in August tying him to the U.S. men's national team through the 2030 World Cup.

United knew him well. He had been a leading candidate for the job in 2022 when Erik ten Hag was ultimately hired. And he left a lasting impression as recently as the summer of 2024 when, under a new sporting leadership, United considered firing Ten Hag and spoke to a range of contenders, Pochettino included.

It was determined then — on both sides — that the timing wasn't right so soon after his brief spell in charge of Chelsea, the person said.

Now, with Pochettino re-energized by his experiences with the U.S., including a run to the round of 16 at this year's World Cup, the timing is right.

United was finalizing the details of Pochettino's appointment on Thursday, with his appointment expected to be confirmed imminently, said the person, who also detailed United's pursuit of the Argentine coach this week.

Work has been underway to conclude the deal once United was made aware of a break clause in Pochettino's recently signed contract, with due diligence carried out before coach Michael Carrick was fired on Thursday.

Confident that Pochettino wanted to take on what has increasingly looked like an impossible job, it was a matter of informing the U.S. soccer federation of its intention to move for a coach, who did so much galvanize the nation during the World Cup. That formal approach came on Wednesday, the night before Carrick was relieved of his duties, the person said.

By that stage rumours had already been swirling around Pochettino and the odds on him to become United's eighth permanent coach or manager in 13 years had been slashed.

There has been criticism of United's handling of the process, making Carrick wait until Thursday to learn his fate that had been long-trailed.

The delay had been due to various reasons. Firstly, no decision could be made until an internal review had been carried out. The person said Carrick had been kept informed about the process.

It wasn't until a meeting with minority owner Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox made the recommendation to change the coach and the decision was made. Berrada and Wilcox returned to Manchester on Wednesday night and rather than inform Carrick by phone, chose to tell him face-to-face at a meeting at the club's training ground on Thursday morning, according to the person's description of events.

It is unlikely to have come as a surprise to Carrick, even if he was less than six months into a two-year contract.

He had overseen United's worst start for 40 years. With only one win in 10 games the 20-time English champion sits 18th in the standings, in the relegation zone.

Another person with knowledge of the decision-making process said the results were simply "not acceptable for Manchester United" and a change had to be made.

The person spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not permitted to do so publicly.

Barring a late hitch, Pochettino's first game in charge will be against Liverpool on Nov. 22.

He will be the latest in a long line of candidates charged with the responsibility of bringing the good times back to a club that for so long dominated English soccer.

It has not won the Premier League title since Ferguson's final season in 2013 and has been overtaken by rivals like Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal.

Pochettino, who won the French title with Paris Saint-Germain and turned Tottenham into a Premier League title challenger, had an underwhelming experience when last in England for one season with Chelsea in 2023-24.

Chelsea ended sixth in the standings, missing out on Champions League qualification and beaten by Liverpool in the final of the English League Cup to leave Pochettino still without a major trophy in English soccer.

Both United and Pochettino will hope that, together, they can snap that streak.

James Robson is at https://x.com/jamesalanrobson

#2772. Jim Harbaugh: Broncos took advantage of a loophole the NFL should not allow

Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is not happy with the way the Broncos backed out of a trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, or with the NFL rules that allowed them to do so.

After agreeing to trade a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Henley, the Broncos told Chargers GM Joe Hortiz they couldn’t go through with it because Henley’s physical revealed concerns about his knee. The Broncos were still willing to trade for Henley, but wanted to give up less. Harbaugh believes physical exams should only be to determine whether or not the player is healthy, not to renegotiate trade terms.

“What happened with the trade? Here’s what I know, from talking to Joe: The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn’t and we didn’t,” Harbaugh said. “In my opinion it’s one of those loopholes that the league should really look into, because it sets a bad precedent.”

Asked if it’s permitted for teams to renegotiate trades after the trade deadline, Harbaugh answered, “It shouldn’t be, but apparently it is. That’s why it’s a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that.”

Harbaugh said the Broncos offered to say Henley passed his physical, but only if the Chargers would take something less than the fifth-round pick the Broncos had agreed to.

“It’s a medical grade. It’s a pass-fail for a medical grade, and they told us they weren’t going to pass him if it’s a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon — they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a fill in the blank. I don’t know what to call that, but that’s what it is,” Harbaugh said.

Harbaugh is right that the NFL has set a bad precedent. By allowing teams to renegotiate trade terms after the deadline, the NFL is incentivizing teams to engage in chicanery on physical exams to squeeze their trade partners into taking less favorable deals. The Chargers refused to budge, but the NFL rules shouldn’t have put the Chargers in a position where they had to make that decision.

#2770. Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi lead The Annika after opening round, Nelly Korda sits two back in return

BELLEAIR, Fla. — Two months later, Nelly Korda didn't miss a beat. She played bogey-free Thursday at The Annika and opened with a 7-under 65 to trail Minami Katsu and Hye-Jin Choi by two shots in her first competition since the Solheim Cup.

"It was nice to kind of feel those juices flowing again, especially playing with Hye-Jin who just had a great round today," Korda said.

She already has clinched LPGA player of the year based on points, and Korda can qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame with a victory in one of the final two events of the season.

Choi, coming off a strong Asia swing that included a pair of runner-up finishes, is looking for her first LPGA title in five years as a member. Her game traveled well from Asia to the Gulf Coast of Florida, with birdies on half her holes for 63.

Katsu played in the afternoon and ran off three straight birdies late in her round to catch Choi at 63. Lindy Duncan was another shot behind with a 64 on a day of low scoring at Pelican Golf Club.

Choi said she can struggle with the Florida grass, especially around the greens. That wasn't a problem Thursday, when she hit 17 greens in regulation.

"I didn't really have like make big mistakes," she said. "I finished really well and I'm really satisfied about making bogey-free round."

Katsu also played bogey-free as she tries to become the sixth Japanese player to win on the LPGA Tour this year.

So much attention was on Korda, the No. 1 player in women's golf who captured two majors early in the season. Her last tournament was the FM Championship outside Boston and then the Solheim Cup, where Korda went 2-1-1 in an American loss in the Netherlands.

"I needed to take that break, and right after Solheim I was burned out," Korda said. "I just needed to mentally step away for a few days."

She typically skips the Asia swing, early and late in the year, and then gears up for the final two LPGA events in Florida.

Korda has four wins this year, but not since the big one — her first U.S. Women's Open title in early June at Riviera. She leads the Race to CME Globe, although next week at the Tour Championship any of the 60 players in the field can become the season champion who gets a $2 million prize.

Also at stake for Korda this week is a chance to surpass Annika Sorenstam, the tournament host, on the career money list. The big carrot is the Hall of Fame, even if she says it's not on her mind.

"Is the Hall of Fame something I'm really looking at? Not at all. I mean, I'm just focusing on being competitive and trying to give it my all," Korda said. "The accolades are great. I'm honored to even be in that position. Honored to be the player of the year.

"What drives me is the competitive tournament that I'm in currently," she said. "I want to do the best that I possibly can where I currently am."

Solheim Cup player Julia Lopez Ramirez of Spain was among four players at 66, while three more players from Europe's winning team — Leona Maguire, Carlota Ciganda and Lottie Woad — were at 65.

#2769. After trade speculation, Colts RB Jonathan Taylor ‘moving on’ to get ready for Miami

The NFL's Tuesday trade deadline came and went, and while other longstanding veteran pillars of the franchise were dealt, Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor somewhat surprisingly remained.

Now, the consensus national reporting leading up to the last 72 hours or so before the trade deadline was that unless the Colts were 'blown away' by either a 'Christian McCaffrey'-esque trade package or even a first round pick in an offer for Taylor, that their star workhorse would remain in Indianapolis.

That being said, when Taylor was asked whether he wanted to be traded, after seeing All-Pro teammates Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner both recently moved elsewhere, he was rather vague on Thursday in his answer—only responding that he was focusing and getting ready to play the Miami Dolphins at home this weekend:

While Taylor had previously indicated that he wanted to retire as a member of the Colts before signing a contract extension in early August, and that he had not requested a trade only a few weeks ago, it's unclear if his mindset or desires changed once the Colts began a fire sale two weeks ago—and have now launched their ongoing rebuild.

On the season, Taylor has 161 carries for 656 total rushing yards (4.1 ypc. avg.) and 8 rushing touchdowns during all 9 starts. He is currently the Colts franchise's all-time leader in rushing touchdowns (77) and trails only Hall of Famer Edgerrin James as the organization's career rushing yards (8,254) and carries (1,712) leader respectively.

Even though Taylor remained a Colts for the remainder of the 2026 campaign, it'll be interesting to see if he still is a member of the franchise this offseason—especially closer to the NFL Draft next spring.

While he's the Colts best player right now and remains an elite Top 5 player at the running back position, it's a fair question with turning 28-years-old in January of whether he still has the prime career longevity left to outlast an Indianapolis rebuild that could (ideally) take only 2-3 years to complete if all goes to according to plan.

As it relates to Miami defending Taylor, they're exactly an average run stopping defense, coming in at 16th league-wide with opposing offenses averaging 111.8 total rushing yards per game.

The fleet-footed South Florida transfer is a limited passer who hasn't cleared 200 passing yards since Week 3. While the TE position goes 12-15 players deep with some really talented players to consider starting in your lineup, Carter's upside is as high as any TE  in the country against the Cowpokes.

Bacheyie was a complete unknown entering the season, but he has proven to be a consistently involved and productive player for a perennially trailing Syracuse team that has allowed 27+ points in five of their last six appearances. While his three 15+ point boom weeks are what CFF managers are looking for, he also has a stable floor, having scored 5+ points in every game besides the goose egg he tossed up against Pitt in Week 3. I think he finds the end zone for a sixth time this season against a retooling NC State that just fired longtime HC Dave Doeren.

Maiava was more potent from a fantasy perspective last season, when he ran for 157 yards and six touchdowns, which is vital in standard four-point passing touchdown formats. However, this season, Maiava has completely stopped running, generating -71 rushing yards with two scores. His passing production has taken a hit as well, clearing 300 passing yards with 2+ touchdowns three times. The UNLV transfer has failed to reach 14 points in three of his last four games and travels across the country to take on the National Champs in a must-win spot to keep USC's playoff hopes alive. He's my P4 QB32 this weekend and best left on your bench until next week when USC welcomes Maryland to The Coliseum.

It was a magnificent, one-game, streaming performance from Washington, who put up a season-high 32.3 points last week versus downtrodden Purdue. He plays Wisconsin's 13th-rated defense this week. The dream is over.

Kansas State has lost its last three games with QB Avery Johnson injured and has been painfully inconsistent in Collin Klein's first season at the helm. While Fields popped off for 16.4 points on 20 carries last week in a 66-28 blowout at the hands of Oklahoma State last weekend, he had scored under ten points in three of his previous four and shares carries with incumbent starter RB Joe Jackson. It's all fun and games when you're churning out yards against one of the many pitiful Big 12 defenses, but this week Fields has to deal with TCU's pretty stout defense that held Baylor to six points, BYU to 17, Kansas to 16 and West Virginia to 24. I simply do not trust this patchwork KSU offense to mount sustained drives and score 20+ points, so I'm sitting Fields this week and am considering giving him a start in Week 13 against Iowa State.

I have nothing but love for the hard-charging Eagles tailback who has taken the Heights by storm with 35.8 points against Georgia Tech and 20.4 last week versus Florida State. But I am exercising caution with BC traveling to play a fired-up ND coming off their big win over Miami. It's only a temporary matchup-based benching, as MacCormack should be back in your lineup next week against Syracuse.

Hiter logged 20 carries in Week 10 and looked ready to take the starting reins from Jordan Marshall last week against in-state rival Michigan State. Unfortunately, he received just six carries for 17 yards and a touchdown, and got passed over in favor of Bryson Kuzdzal, who converted his nine carries into 49 yards in the embarrassing 15-6 loss to the Spartans last weekend. We cannot trust any of Michigan's running backs right now, and I think you should liquidate all your Wolverine RB shares since they play UCLA next week and Ohio State to end the year.

A preseason top-25 wideout, Craver is a slot-heavy receiver who was banged up a few weeks ago and has not regained his form since returning. We've seen 57% of his routes within nine yards of the line of scrimmage with a 6.9-yard ADOT. This kind of usage explains his pedestrian 9.1 YPC while scoring less than five points in four out of his last five games. A&M takes on an excellent Tennessee defense that is pitching three-and-outs 42% of the time while creating 17 turnovers and ranking second in FBS in yards per dropback allowed (4.7). Throw in his accuracy-challenged quarterback, Marcel Reed, and I am confident that Craver is worth benching in Week 11.

Barnes was incredibly explosive on a per-play basis last year at Wake Forest, leading to rampant optimism when he transferred to OSU and HC Eric Morris. Unfortunately, Drew Mestamaker's roommate, Miles Coleman, has taken over the WR3 role and has accrued at least 69 receiving yards in four of his last five appearances. Looks like we will have to wait on Barnes' breakout for another year.

The hopes for a top-10 TE campaign from Brahmer have been dashed, as he hasn't scored 8.0+ points in eight of nine games so far. His lone 22.4-point explosion came way back in Week 2 against lowly Temple, with Andrew Rappleya surpassing him as the most productive Nittany Lions TE. Brahmer has devolved into waiver fodder, much to my chagrin.

With Oakley reeling in just one of his four targets last week against Oklahoma State, I cannot trust this Kansas State pass game and, by proxy, Oakley himself.

#2759. Can Warriors survive without Stephen Curry with tough stretch ahead?

On Thursday, the Golden State Warriors announced that star guard Steph Curry was diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be shelved for at least the next two weeks. The 38-year-old suffered the injury midway through the first quarter of Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets.

For a team and organization that has orbited around Curry's generational gravity for nearly two decades, the loss is significant. Prior to Wednesday's loss (Curry played just five minutes), he had been averaging near-identical production to his 2016 MVP season.

The 18-year veteran has been able to shoulder a seismic load — due to the absence of Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis' abrupt decision to step away from basketball citing health reasons — handling the ball more than ever and converting shots at the most efficient rate, all while minimizing turnovers. Curry has been the driving force for the 8-4 Warriors, who have won eight of their past nine games, which is nothing short of a testament to his greatness amid a loaded Western Conference and a team that, on paper, pales in comparison to its peers.

The Warriors will be without Stephen Curry for at least two weeks.

The Warriors' next seven games offer quite the challenge. In the coming fortnight, Golden State will face San Antonio, Dallas, Memphis, Boston and Portland, which have all won more than 60% of their games to date. But amid those upcoming hurdles, there's a strong belief within the locker room that the roster as-is can withstand Curry's absence in the short term.

"The spirit of this team is better," forward Draymond Green said to reporters following the game. "We're more certain of who we are, what makes us a good team. That puts us in a better position to be successful without him as opposed to where we were last year."

Green's assessment checks out. In 317 non-Curry minutes, the Warriors have been able to outscore teams by 14 points, according to PBP Stats, a substantial improvement from last season (Golden State lost those minutes by a whopping 135 points). The improvement of fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski, who will now come into focus as the team's biggest perimeter threat, will be tested in the interim. Albeit in a much-smaller role alongside Curry, Podziemski has been able to clean up his shot profile and ball security, two areas of focus for him since he was drafted in 2023. This season, Podz has taken on a much larger playmaking role when Curry is off the floor and is able to draw more fouls — in addition to excelling in transition and off-ball activity.

There's also the presence of rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, a Swiss Army knife of a combo forward that is equal parts thrilling and chaotic, who has taken on enough responsibility early on and converted his chances at veteran-level clips, currently in the 87th percentile of rim success and 79th in perimeter success, according to Cleaning the Glass. The first-year phenom is the team's second-leading scorer, averaging 21.7 points per game.

If the Warriors are to survive these next two weeks, they'll need to further emphasize their unselfish identity. Without Curry's gravity, ball movement becomes even more of a premium. They're second in passes made, third in assists and first in secondary assists because of a starting lineup that possesses five players who can create with the ball in their hands to varying degrees (Lendeborg, Podziemski, Al Horford, Draymond Green and the insertion of De'Anthony Melton, who likely picks up the minutes void and is a capable creator on his own).

(Melton's presence also juices the Warriors' penchant for forcing turnovers. They're surprisingly ninth in half-court defensive efficiency, fifth in opponent turnover rate and are good at turning mistakes into points, eighth-best at the time of this writing.)

The most important factor, however, during this period of uncertainty, is the leadership structure between Green and Kerr. Those two and Curry have been the lone constants over the years, and with Curry gone, Green and Kerr should be the consistent go-tos for guidance and morale.

They share a deep understanding and longevity that transcend most partnerships in sports. And they aren't new to uncomfortable situations — whether it's internal drama, injuries, or the growing pains that come with two-timeline situations.

"I was thrilled that the guys stayed together," Kerr said after Wednesday's game. "It's a great group to coach. I really love this team and I'm excited about what's ahead."

Make no mistake, Curry's absence, even if it's for two weeks, will be felt every time this team steps on the floor. But the energy about this new group, despite the lack of outside expectations, is tangible and might just be enough to hold down the fort until 30 is ready to go again.

#2757. Aaron Brewer’s Absence Crushes Dolphins’ Offensive Line Hopes

The Miami Dolphins' offensive line was supposed to be the team's saving grace this year. Instead, it has become the biggest source of frustration for fans and coaches alike. Now, the group faces a fresh setback just days before a critical matchup. Center Aaron Brewer missed his second straight practice on Thursday due to a concussion. Sports Illustrated reports that Brewer appears unlikely to face the Indianapolis Colts this Sunday. This news effectively shuts the door on any hope of stability for the Dolphins' front five.

There was genuine excitement when the team drafted Kadyn Proctor and brought back Brewer after his All-Pro season in 2025. Those moves suggested the unit would take a massive leap forward. That progress never happened. The run blocking showed promise for a brief stretch around the bye week, but the pass protection remains a disaster. Malik Willis's struggles were largely caused by poor pass protection, according to Sports Illustrated. Receivers missed routes, and Willis hesitated, but the line failed to hold its blocks.

The rankings from Pro Football Focus tell a harsh story about the current state of the group. Brewer sits at 17th out of 36 qualifying centers. That is not terrible, but it is far below his 2025 standard. Right tackle Austin Jackson ranks 71st out of 71 tackles. Jonah Savaiinaea lands at number 69. The only player with a decent grade is left tackle Patrick Paul at 47th. The rest of the line simply cannot get the job done.

With Brewer out, third-year player Andrew Meyer is almost certain to start at center. This is a massive blow to an offense that already lacks rhythm. Meyer has not shown he can handle the pressure of a starting role in the NFL. Rookie guard Kadyn Proctor faced a similar issue, missing the Week 8 matchup versus the New England Patriots because a concussion prevented any practice. The team cannot keep losing key players to the same injury bug. It creates a cycle of disruption that the coaching staff cannot fix.

The Dolphins have other issues to deal with, including the return of defensive tackle Keith Cooper Jr. and the search for a new quarterback. But the offensive line remains the anchor dragging the team down. Expectations were that improvement would begin during the season's final weeks. Losing Brewer against Indianapolis kills that hope. With a 1-7 record, the Dolphins currently rank No. 3 for securing the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. A loss to the Colts on Sunday, Nov. 15, would only add to the misery of a broken offensive line.

#2756. Knoxville, Chattanooga Fox affiliates pass on Titans game, for now

The Tennessee Titans apparently need an asterisk on their name.

At least two TV markets in the state for which the team is named have passed on televising their Week 10 game against the Jaguars.

Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing explains that 506sports.com coverage map shows that the Knoxville and Chattanooga Fox affiliates will not televise the Jaguars-Titans game. Instead, Vikings-Packers will be shown in the 1:00 p.m. ET window.

It’s a preliminary map, as Lerner notes. The Fox affiliates in Knoxville and Chattanooga, the third- and fourth-largest cities in the league by way of population, could change their minds.

It’s not personal, it’s business. And the affiliates think they’re business interests are best served by showing Packers-Vikings not Jaguars-Titans.

LeBron James will sit out his third game of the early 2026-27 season for the Philadelphia 76ers' matchup with the Toronto Raptors on Thursday.

James is listed on the Sixers' injury report as out with "low back/sciatica management," which has been the reason he's sat two of Philadelphia's previous 12 games this season.

However, the Sixers do play back-to-back games on Sunday and Monday, hosting the Indiana Pacers then visiting the Brooklyn Nets.

So far this season, James is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.5 assists on 43% shooting from the floor. Embiid is scoring 17.7 points per game with 9.3 rebounds and 3.8 assists. He is also shooting 37%, while making only 4 of 33 (12%) 3-point attempts.

If Embiid doesn't play, Philadelphia will be short-handed at center with Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction) also out for Thursday.

#2752. Giants vs. Commanders weather forecast: How inclement conditions could impact NFC East showdown

The New York Giants and Washington Commanders will do battle on Thursday night, but they won't just be battling each other in the NFC East showdown.

Ahead of kickoff, it's looking like there will be poor weather conditions throughout the contest.

According to several reporters on the ground, it is already raining heavily at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

MORE: Best bets for Thursday Night Football in Week 10

"It is currently pouring at MetLife Stadium with some thunder and lightning mixed in," The Athletic's Dan Duggan wrote.

The lightning is important to note because the NFL will delay a game if there is lightning within 10 miles of the stadium.

That leaves open the possibility this game gets delayed, either before or during the contest.

A Washington Commanders helmet on the sidelines in the second half against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

According to Accuweather.com, the rain is expected throughout the contest, although it is slated to be heaviest in the first hour of the game before lightening up a bit later on.

Wind is expected to remain steady at about 10-12 MPH, with gusts not exceeding 14 MPH. Anything over 15 MPH usually impacts the ball in the air.

The good news is, the temperatures won't be frigid and should sit around 50 degrees throughout the game.

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) reacts after defeating the Houston Texans in overtime at Reliant Stadium. Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The big concern with this particular forecast is the rain. Slick conditions make it harder to grip the football, which could lead to more drops and fumbles.

Because of the rain, we may also see a reduction in passing attempts and that would mean more work for the running backs on each team, including Giants rusher Cam Skattebo and Commanders backs Austin Ekeler and Rachaad White.

With the wind expected to be under 15 MPH, neither the kicking games nor the passing attacks should be impacted.

MORE: Bold predictions for Thursday Night Football in NFL Week 10

Inclement conditions like the ones expected on Thursday night typically lead to fewer points, so don't expect too many fireworks.

#2750. NFL Injury Report, Week 10: Latest news, updates for Puka Nacua, George Pickens, more players for fantasy football

It's the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season and by now you likely have weathered plenty of injuries on your fantasy football rosters. We have a handful of big names we're tracking going into Week 10 while four teams are on bye — the Bears, Broncos, Buccaneers and Eagles. Below we'll update you on the latest injury news, plus provide some useful fantasy football analysis.

Sam Darnold, SEA (quad/ribs) — Out for Week 10

Drew Lock, SEA (oblique) — Should be good to start

Deshaun Watson, CLE (concussion) — Set to start

Gardner Minshew, ARI (elbow) — On IR with torn UCL

Mahomes: At the time of Mahomes' injury in Week 9, it looked as though we were watching a QB who may be done for the season. But after exiting due to an elbow injury, Mahomes was able to return in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Mahomes completed 23-of-31 passes for 242 yards and two scores, posting fewer than 20 fantasy points for the fifth time in the past six games.

Kenneth Walker III continues to be the focal point of the offense as the passing game lacks depth and a vertical threat. The Chiefs face the Falcons in Week 10 and Mahomes was a full practice participant Wednesday, a good sign for him being able to play. If he's able to go, it'll be a chance for him to work with new receiver Josh Downs, who came over in a trade with the Colts on Tuesday.

Seahawks QBs: Head coach Mike Macdonald already went on the radio Monday and said Darnold will be out Week 10 against the Raiders. Lock underwent tests on an oblique injury he suffered Sunday and those came back "good," so he's in line to start again. The Raiders have been a great fantasy matchup for QBs this season, allowing the fifth-most points to the position. However, the Seattle offense has struggled a bit with lack of depth behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock is back in the QB2 streaming convo for Sunday and isn't a bad spot start if you have Caleb Williams or Bo Nix on bye.

Minshew: The Cardinals QB is on IR with a torn UCL. That means rookie Carson Beck will start. If you remember back to the preseason, Beck was actually pretty good. There's a chance this is a good move overall for the offense, particularly TE Trey McBride. But Arizona is down WR Michael Wilson (neck) and Beck won't have many other options in the passing game. In Superflex, Beck is worth a speculative add to see how he does in Week 10 against the Rams.

Willis: The Dolphins surprised us before the trade deadline by placing Willis on IR, which could mean he's done for the season this late in the year. He'll miss at least the next four games, which would mean the soonest he could be back is Week 14 against Chicago. 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord is the backup and will start in Week 10 versus the Colts. Brady Cook will be the backup.

Miami's passing offense enters Week 10 ranked 30th in the NFL. Chances are it doesn't get much better with McCord under center, but we'll need to see. It's a downgrade to receivers like Malik Washington, Greg Dulcich and Caleb Douglas in the short term until we assess things. Ollie Gordon II could be leaned on a bit more, and McCord may use the RB and Dulcich as safety valves.

TreVeyon Henderson, NE (illness — ruled out)

Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Report: Out a max of three weeks

Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Chance to return this week

Bhayshul Tuten, JAX (ankle/foot) — DNP on Wednesday

Etienne: This is one to watch going into the weekend. Etienne got in a limited practice on Thursday and will likely hold a questionable tag going into Sunday's game versus the Panthers. If Etienne is active, he could be on some sort of pitch count. But he could still leech some touches away from Audric Estime, who was a trending waiver-wire add this week. Alvin Kamara also got nine touches last week against the Browns. Estime likely leads the backfield with Etienne out. But if the veteran returns, it could water down the touches between the three backs.

Patriots RBs: Stevenson exited Sunday's blowout loss to the Packers early and did not return. Henderson has missed the past two games after being hospitalized due to "unexplained neurological symptoms." Stevenson missed practice Wednesday and was limited on Thursday, but will reportedly be sidelined multiple weeks.

The Patriots face the Lions in Germany this week, which means Corey Kiner is likely to take over as the lead back. He finished with a solid 8-55-1 rushing line against Green Bay, though most of that production was on a fourth-quarter drive when the game was essentially over. Lan Larison would be the RB2 for New England. Keep an eye on this as Stevenson getting back on the practice field Thursday is telling. Maybe there's a shot he's active. But if he's out, Kiner is a decent RB3/flex play.

Jacobs: On the other side of that game, Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the win over the Patriots and didn't return. Rushing duties were then split between Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson with MarShawn Lloyd out. Johnson rushed for 68 yards on 14 carries with a score. He looked pretty good running the ball for a team that has struggled to do so all season. But it was also in a blowout. Even so, Johnson is a proactive add off the waiver wire with Jacobs expected to miss time. Green Bay faces the Vikings in Week 10 before the bye and it would be hard to trust any Packers RB against one of the best defenses in the NFL. Johnson will be a risky flex play against Minnesota in Week 10. Strong isn't a bad add in deeper PPR formats and keep an eye on Lloyd, who could be back soon.

Puka Nacua, LAR (knee/turf toe) — To miss "significant" time

Michael Wilson, ARI (neck) — Out for season

Luther Burden III, CHI (concussion) — on bye

Nacua: Sean McVay told reporters Wednesday that the wideout will avoid IR for now but miss "significant" time with knee sprains and turf toe. The Rams are already without Davante Adams, but McVay did offer hope that the veteran WR could return from a ruptured hamstring as soon as Week 13. For now, there isn't much WR depth. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and the trio of tight ends — Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen — will need to step up. We'd throw Terrance Ferguson into that group, but he remains on IR and isn't expected back in Week 10. L.A. should lean more on its run game with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

With Nacua out, it's a downgrade to the passing game and Matthew Stafford's fantasy outlook. It's a slight bump up for Williams and Corum, both of whom are involved in the passing game plenty. The Rams take on the Cardinals before their bye in Week 11, which is an easy draw for the run game. Mumpfield isn't a bad waiver wire add, along with Atwell in deeper formats. But don't expect any receiver to get the type of volume like Nacua did.

#2749. What Jamahl Mosley said about bad body language before Dejounte Murray’s crashout

What Jamahl Mosley said about bad body language before Dejounte Murray's crashout appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New Orleans Pelicans have a problem that extends beyond missed shots, blown defensive assignments, and embarrassing losses. Frustration is spilling into public view, exposing cracks in a locker room still searching for an identity under Jamahl Mosley. Dejounte Murray's now-deleted social media accusations of 'sabotage' have only intensified questions about the team's chemistry, accountability, and leadership.

Perhaps most concerning is that Mosley warned about the dangers of negative body language after the first four-game losing streak of the season, and even had a prescription for curing those ills.

"One is not to overreact. And when I talk about body language, you know, nobody's going to be happy to be (losing). I don't want nobody sitting around whistling and singing happy songs," Mosley admitted to ClutchPoints. "So, there's a mood that you can have with not getting the result that you want in those moments."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"There's also a way that you bounce out of it," Mosley added. "Then that becomes the encouragement to your teammate when they check in the game, when they check out the game. You now have to fill somebody else up with the encouragement when they step into the game, and that's how that energy can transfer over."

Unfortunately, the Pelicans have been put on blast for some lackadaisical, uninspired play. This squad just ran through perhaps the worst three-game stretch in franchise history, per point differential. There was no energy in the Smoothie King Center as the Brooklyn Nets wrapped up a 145-111 win because the fans had left before the fourth quarter started.

Then Murray went on to Twitter to argue about film study and play design.

Social media was pure electricity as the skeptics ran through the film study. An account highlighted the team's 1-8 record with Murray in the lineup this season compared with 3-0 without him. Murray responded by writing that the post sounded like someone from inside the organization had prompted it and declaring, "THE SABOTAGE IS REAL!"

It was quite the 180 from training camp for the 30-year-old.

"I never live my life worrying about what somebody that's not in these rooms is saying," Murray told ClutchPoints at Media Day. "And then again, if that's your job, that's your job."

"I'm somebody who understands that all you guys have a job in this room. You know what I'm saying? So if Dejounte was turning the ball over, that's your job to be like, man, you got to take care of the damn ball," he added. "You know, if Dejounte had a great game, I feel like it's your job to (report that as well)…I think it should be more about criticizing how we play than who we are as a person. I respect you guys job. I just think when it gets personal, that's where the problems come from. But criticize me. Good, bad, it doesn't matter when it comes to the game of basketball."

The eye in the sky and ball don't lie, and deleted tweets won't kill the soap opera conversations. The very public frustration has coincided with rumors of friction between Murray and Mosley, whom the Pelicans hired in the offseason after his five-year tenure with the Orlando Magic. Murray is averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists in nine games, well below his All-Star form, and has ceded touches to second-year guard Jeremiah Fears.

Mosley's comments preceded Murray's now-deleted posts. They must be addressed, though. The accusation, whether intended seriously or as an emotional response to criticism, immediately created a controversy larger than the team's win/loss record or his declining stats.

A missed assignment does not excuse the next missed assignment. Getting pulled from a game does not eliminate the responsibility to support the player checking in. Frustration is understandable. Allowing it to undermine teammates is another matter entirely. By most accounts, Murray's social media account specifically, this situation is teetering on toxic.

Mosley, to his credit, has consistently framed body language as a teachable moment rather than a symptom of fracture. His public stance suggests a coach attempting to thread a needle of validating the frustration of losing while demanding that players convert that emotion into energy for one another rather than allowing it to curdle into something more corrosive. Whether that message lands in a locker room now confronting a very public airing of internal suspicion is anyone's guess.

#2747. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2746. Kane hungry for more after England caps record

Harry Kane pledged he would play for England "for as long as I can" after winning a record 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

The England captain scored from the penalty spot as Thomas Tuchel's team won 2-1 at Wembley to guarantee a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

The 33-year-old, who won the Ballon d'Or last month, moved clear of former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who won 125 caps during his long career.

Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions captain, along with Football Association patron Prince William.

A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of Kane and the words "England's Finest".

The skipper, who showed off his Ballon d'Or trophy to the Wembley crowd before the match, described the occasion as "incredible".

"I was trying to play it cool, I was trying to not smile too much, not give away too much emotion," he said. "Obviously I try to stay focused on the job."

Kane added: "I don't know if any of this has sunk in, to be honest with you, maybe in the winter break when I've got a couple of weeks off.

"I'll be on the beach somewhere and we'll try and reflect on everything that I've achieved, because these ones are probably the biggest in my career, without a doubt."

The Bayern Munich forward said he was inspired by the example set by Croatia veteran Luka Modric, 41, who came on as a late substitute at Wembley.

"That inspires me to push the limits," he said. "Like with him, I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you.

"Everyone's journey is different, for sure, but... as long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I'm performing at the highest level, then I'll be here for as long as I can.

"Whether that's until I'm 40 or not, we'll have to wait and see, but right now, yeah, I'm enjoying every moment."

#2745. Recent history shows that 49ers-Cowboys is a ‘rivalry’ in name only

The San Francisco 49ers head to Arlington to face off with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in what used to be a hotly contested rivalry. Yes, you read that right. Of course, both fan bases and the players dislike each other given the history, but a rivalry isn't a rivalry until a team wins a game. I'm referring to the 49ers owning the Cowboys.

Despite numerous beatdowns, the Cowboys (Micah Parsons) players and organization have stated they will "have something" next time for the 49ers. Ok, when? One side does the winning; the other side does the yapping.

Here is the recent history between Dallas and San Francisco. The 49ers lead the all-time series with a 21-19-1 record over 41 meetings. The last Cowboys victory was in 2020 over the Nick Mullens-led 49ers.

The two teams squared off in the playoffs for the first time since the 49ers defeated Dallas to move on to the Super Bowl in the 1994 NFC Championship Game. Jimmy Garoppolo and the 49ers narrowly escaped with a 23-17 score following a mental lapse by Dak Prescott, allowing the game to end before an attempted spike.

Deebo Samuel was the engine of the 49ers' offense and famously told Kyle Shanahan to get him the ball, and he "put the ball in the box."

In back-to-back seasons, the two franchises met, but this time at Levi's Stadium. The entire game was tense and went down to the wire, with one of the more interesting play calls and formations for Dallas being Ezekiel Elliott snapping the ball alone and being asked to block the pass rush on the final play.

With a 19-12 score, Brock Purdy and the 49ers did enough to advance to the NFC Championship Game in Philadelphia. The 49ers' victory tied the all-time series at 19-19-1.

The 2023 49ers were a juggernaut. Dallas stood no chance against the 49ers offense, and George Kittle lit the Cowboys up for three touchdowns and proudly displayed a shirt that expresses every 49ers fan's sentiments regarding Dallas.

The 32-point margin was the largest victory over the Cowboys. Parsons would run to his podcast to complain about Kittle rather than stop him. That is typical Cowboy behavior.

Dallas actually led this contest at halftime, 10-6. The third quarter would see the floodgates open for the 49ers offense, and the team put up 21 in the quarter. Kittle would score again, and Dallas would close the gap with 3:32 left in the fourth quarter, but ultimately the 49ers would prevail.

Anders Carlson was the 49ers' kicker in this game and added three field goals. Just something funny to note.

Unfortunately, until the Cowboys punch back, this rivalry has turned into a one-sided beef. It won't happen Sunday. The rivalry has turned into an avalanche.

Years ago, Sandro Mamukelashvili began his career as a member of the Milwaukee Bucks, where he spent his first 1.5 NBA seasons after they drafted him 54th overall in 2021. But in March of 2023, they waived him before he joined the San Antonio Spurs for 2.5 years then ultimately established himself with the Toronto Raptors in 2025-26.

He parlayed that breakout campaign into a four-year, $52 million deal with the Los Angeles Lakers this past summer and has been absolutely sensational to begin the season. On Wednesday against the Bucks, he authored one of his best games thus far with 23 points (9-of-15 shooting, 5-of-8 from deep), three rebounds, two assists and one steal. In the win, Los Angeles outscored Milwaukee by 21 points during his 26 minutes.

Following the victory — the Lakers' seventh in a row — Mamukelashvili didn't pass up the opportunity to point out what Milwaukee lost when it parted ways with him years ago.

"I'm happy we got this dub," he said postgame. "Even though I got drafted here, it's always great to come back and beat the team that waived you."

Mamukelashvili has been among the league's top reserves this season, elevating the Lakers' offense with his shooting, passing, driving and transition ball-handling. They deploy him in a variety of lineups, where he spends time at both power forward and center. According to databallr, they're scoring 128.1 points per 100 possessions when he's on the floor.

Regardless of whether he's sharing the court with Walker Kessler, the Lakers are thriving in his minutes, which allows them to slot him among the starters or help anchor bench-heavy units — the result of his size and wide-ranging offensive skill-set.

Los Angeles gets a few days off before concluding its road trip Sunday evening against the Phoenix Suns at 7 p.m., when it aims for an eighth straight win. Averaging 23 points, 5.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.0 steals over his past two outings, Mamukelashvili will hope to stay in a groove himself and keep helping the 11-2 Lakers stack victories.

"But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel?

A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma

But the German added: "It's not personal. We will never assume Cole is in the mindset never to come to the camp.

Kane's top 10 England moments - which was your favourite?

#2728. How early-season shot selection shifts are impacting fantasy basketball value

We're far enough into the season to notice something useful, as long as we're careful about what we're measuring. Scoring averages and shooting percentages can swing a lot over the first few weeks. Where a player takes his shots tends to settle faster, so it's a better place to start.

In testing this for 2025-26, Tall Order Digital found that among 156 qualifying players, shot-zone shares over the first four games correlated with the rest of the season at 0.72 to 0.86 (a perfect match would be 1.0). Field-goal percentage correlated at just 0.46.

To see what the shifts are doing to fantasy basketball value, I've listed each player's preseason ADP next to his current 9-cat rank (through Nov. 11). Shot data is Basketball-Reference totals as of Nov. 11, compared with last season or a career mark.

Luka Dončić and De'Aaron Fox are ranked higher than where they were drafted, and Michael Porter Jr. has climbed despite scoring less. In all three cases, the revised shot profiles are landing and netting positive results.

He's launching 13.4 3s a game, up from 10.8 last season (which led the NBA). His 3-point share has risen from .476 to .549, and last year's .476 was already a career high. The bigger move is at the rim, where his share has dropped from .076 to .060. He's making 40.8% of his 3s and averaging 38.6 points in 11 games.

Fox is getting to the line far more often. He's attempted 53 free throws on 111 field-goal attempts, a free-throw rate of .477, compared with .235 last season and a .316 career mark. His career high is .420, set in 2019-20, so this is a new peak.

It isn't coming from more shots at the rim, though. His rim share is flat (.207 vs .201). What changed is the middle of the floor. Shots from 3-10 feet jumped from .204 to .315 of his attempts, while long twos nearly vanished (.067 to .018). He's also attempting 3.1 3s a game, down from 5.5, so his average shot is 12.4 feet from the basket instead of 14.4.

He's traded long twos and 3s for more floaters and short jumpers, and the whistle is doing the rest. He's backing it up with 51% shooting and 6.2 assists, though his scoring is 14.2 points, down from 18.6.

Porter is taking 3s on .615 of his attempts, up from .506 last season. He had never topped .556 in a season. His free-throw rate has climbed from .237 to .349, and his 10-to-16-foot share has collapsed from .075 to .018. He's averaging 21.5 points, below last season's 24.2, yet he's still up five spots in his draft position. A more interesting shot profile doesn't automatically mean more points. Playing alongside a player like Julius Randle likely also affects how a player navigates getting shots up.

These two are still scoring, but their rank has dropped since they were drafted. A new shot mix doesn't always show up the same way in the box score.

Durant is a free-throw story. His FTr has risen from .339 to .582 (92 attempts in 12 games, 7.7 a game), above his previous career best of .523 in 2012-13 and his .392 career mark. His 3-point volume has fallen from 5.8 a game to 3.8, and he's turning it over 3.3 times a game. Durant is at 20.9 points on 49% shooting. Having Fred VanVleet back and running more offense through Alperen Şengün is putting less dependency on Durant – which is probably a good thing in the long run. Fantasy-wise, Jabari Smith Jr. and Şengün's growth has Durant adjusting his shot profile, which could lessen his value as a scorer.

Gilgeous-Alexander's rim share has fallen from 22.8% to 13.1% and his 10-to-16-foot share has risen from .273 to .303. His 3s are up to .292 on 6.7 attempts a game from .226 on 4.4 last season. SGA's free-throw rate has dropped from .465 to .339. He's still scoring 29.7 a night, so this is a small slide from a very high perch.

That's an observable redistribution that likely comes down to how much attention he's drawing without co-stars Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren to balance out the Thunder's offensive attack. SGA is having to settle for more contested shots and rely more on his jumper. SGA has proven to be one of the most efficient guards in the league, but fantasy managers may have to accept that this could be a down season. He's shooting 45.6% from the field as of Wednesday.

This is where the shot shift is costing the most fantasy value. A big jump in one kind of shot usually takes a few weeks to settle and the efficiency tends to lag the volume. Whether that's what's happening here, or whether the new role simply isn't a good fit, is something we'll know more as we move further into the season.

In 10 games with Orlando, 100 of his 148 attempts have been 3s: 67.6%. His 3-point share had slid from .543 as a rookie to .354 last season, against a .441 career mark. His two-point attempts have fallen from 9.5 a game to 4.8 this season. His average shot distance is 23.4 feet, up from 13.5.

The results haven't been good: 39.2% from the field and 18.0 points a game, down from 20.1. The key question is whether Orlando keeps asking him to operate on such a narrow diet. If it does, last season's scoring profile may be the wrong baseline even after his shooting recovers.

Markkanen has the second-biggest 3-point jump on this list, making up .646 of his attempts, up from .402 last season. His previous career high was .570 in 2024-25. His rim share has halved, from .210 to .106, and his average shot distance has gone from 13.9 feet to 18.9. And now, he'll miss at least a month with two non-displaced fractures in his shooting hand.

He's scoring 18.0 points a game on 39% shooting, down from 26.7 in 42 games last season. A bigger share of 3s didn't produce more points here, at least so far.

Buzelis is a different case from the others in this group, because his shot mix barely changed. His 3s are .520 of his attempts, almost identical to last year's .514. What changed is how many shots he's taking. He's down from 12.5 field-goal attempts a game to about 9.8, with both his 3s (6.4 to about 5.1) and his twos (6.1 to about 4.7) falling, and his minutes slipped from 29.2 to 26.3.

His free-throw rate jumped from .247 to .429, but that's partly a smaller denominator. He's getting to the line about 4.2 times a game, up from 3.1, on far fewer shots. The extra trips haven't made up for the lost volume. He's shooting 43% with 2.8 turnovers, and he's ranked 226th. A higher free-throw rate doesn't help much when the shots aren't there to begin with. Caleb Wilson has a fractured hand and is reportedly expected to miss 4-6 weeks, so expect Buzelis to see a short-term boost in his volume.

Shot diets settle faster than shooting percentages, and that's the lens for this group. Bane and Markkanen have the clearest case: 3s are 68% and 65% of their shots, and that's likely to stick, while their 39% shooting is the part more likely to improve. More 3s  also means a lower field-goal percentage but more 3PM, so expect a trade-off in 9-cat rather than a clear gain.

Fox and Durant are getting to the line at career-high rates, which gives them some cushion on off nights, though it hasn't lifted either one's rank. Buzelis is the caution. His free-throw rate is up, but his shot volume is down, so the better rate hasn't helped his fantasy value.

Bet on the shot profile, then check whether the production is catching up.
